switched up sides like a larper that larps Oliver tree💔 .  #animalhospital #foryoupage #idk #shitpost #xybca  In Animal Hospital, you and up to three other players work at a hospital for animals. The main gameplay consists of checking in animals, scanning them for health conditions, and providing the correct Treatments while detecting and avoiding Anomalies. Classes Main article: Classes Classes are modifiers that can give the player specific starting stats, items or additional utility and function. You start the game with the free Intern class, as you play and earn Animal Coins, you can purchase more classes. Some available classes are the Nurse, Secretary, Surgeon, and Doctor. Upon being bought, classes will start at Level 1 and can be upgraded with exp earned by doing shifts, which will improve the buffs earned with the class. Each class comes with its own unique character, Skins, stats and abilities. There are 10 classes in the game. Some classes, like Secret Agent, cost Robux. Anomalies Main article: Anomalies Anomalies are creatures that roam the hospital which can attack and kill patients, visitors, and players. It’s your job to keep the hospital safe, the patients alive, and the anomalies to a minimum. You can fend off anomalies by using your taser (unlocked during Shift 4) and the gun, which can be brought from the store. You can use these items before an anomaly attacks or while it attacks. Sanity Main article: Sanity Sanity is one of the main Mechanics in Animal Hospital. Starting sanity can vary by class, and some classes affect how you can receive sanity both positively and negatively. The coffee and chocolate bar provide an increase to sanity. You can lose sanity by seeing a cursed photo, job stress, encountering Events, such as the ritual, or Enemies like the Stalker or Ghosts. Shifts Main article: Shifts Shifts are periods of time where you must deal with patients that enter the hospital. Shifts start by checking patients in, which then get treated according to their health conditions. At the end of the first four shifts, Dr. Harlow comes in and unlocks features for you, such as the shutter door and cameras, the taser, the emergency wing, a shop where you can buy various items at the start of each shift. Events are unlocked overtime such as fires, death rituals, and emergencies, where an influx of patients rush in, some in critical condition and some anomalies. When a patient is in critical condition, you only have a certain amount of time until they die. Examples of critical patients include: Those undergoing surgeries. Visitors that have fainted. Patients that are on fire. Patients that are being used for a death ritual. You may also encounter special patients like Ratthew and Ron from Accounting. Additionally, characters like Barney and Liz will show up in your shifts with special requests. These two characters are untreatable and do not ask you to check them in.

Braised Chicken Legs with Rice, Potatoes & Veggies🍗 Ingredients * 1 package chicken drumsticks (6–7 pieces) * 1-2 tbsp olive oil * 1 tsp salt * 1 tsp black pepper * 2 tsp garlic powder * 2 tsp onion powder * 2 tsp paprika * ½ tsp cumin * 1 jalapeño, diced * ½ red onion, diced * 1 tbsp sun-dried tomato paste * 1 tbsp @Loisa sofrito * 5–6 garlic cloves, minced * 4 cups chicken stock * 1 (8 oz) can tomato sauce * Small potatoes, halved (about 10–12 baby potatoes) * 1 zucchini, diced * Cooked white rice, for serving (let me know if you guys want my rice recipe) Instructions: 1. Clean the chicken with vinegar, then pat completely dry with paper towels. 2. Season the chicken with the salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, and cumin. Toss until evenly coated. 3. Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or deep skillet over medium-high heat. 4. Brown the chicken for 2–3 minutes per side until golden. It doesn’t need to be cooked through. Remove and set aside. 5. In the same pot, add the diced jalapeño and red onion. Cook for about 5 minutes until softened. 6. Stir in the sun-dried tomato paste and cook for 30 seconds. 7. Add the Loisa Sofrito and minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. 8. Pour in the chicken stock and tomato sauce, stirring to combine. Bring to a gentle boil. 9. Return the chicken to the pot. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 1 hour, or until the chicken is fall-apart tender and the sauce has reduced. 10. About 20 minutes before the chicken is done, add the halved potatoes and diced zucchini. Continue simmering until the potatoes are fork-tender and the zucchini is cooked. 11. Serve over fluffy white rice and spoon plenty of the sauce over the top. #chickenlegs #braised #onepotmeals #cookwithme

EASY MEALS FOR 2 EP 22 Crispy Gochujang Chicken Thighs Ingredients Really a meal for 1 because someone ate all of it :)  Chicken * 400–450 g boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces * 1/2 teaspoon salt * 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder * 1/2 teaspoon black pepper * 3 tablespoons cornstarch * 3–4 tablespoons neutral oil, for shallow-frying, enough to cover bottom of pan  Spicy gochujang sauce * 1 tbsp butter  * 1½ tablespoons gochujang * 1 tablespoon soy sauce * 1 tablespoon brown sugar * 1 tablespoon rice vinegar * 2 teaspoons sesame oil * 3 cloves garlic, finely minced * 1 teaspoon grated ginger * 1/4 cup water For serving * Steamed rice * Sliced green onion * Toasted sesame seeds * Cucumber, optional Instructions 1. Pat the chicken thighs dry and cut them into bite-sized pieces. Season with salt, garlic powder, black pepper. 2. Add the cornstarch and toss until the chicken is evenly coated with a thin, dry layer. 3. Heat the neutral oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken in a single layer and shallow-fry for 4–5 minutes per side, or until golden, crispy and cooked through. Work in batches if necessary. 4. Transfer the chicken to a plate. Carefully remove the oil, add butter to skillet. 5. Reduce the heat to medium-low. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for about 30 seconds. 6. Stir in the gochujang, soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, sesame oil, water and optional gochugaru. Simmer for 1–2 minutes, stirring, until glossy and slightly thickened. 7. Return the chicken to the skillet and toss for 30–60 seconds, until evenly coated. Don’t cook it in the sauce for too long or the coating will soften. 8. Serve immediately over rice and finish with green onion and sesame seeds. #chicken #koreanchicken #cooking #EasyRecipe #creatorsearchinsights

Prepare the wet batter by whisking together buttermilk, garlic powder, black pepper, salt, and smoked paprika. Add the chicken strips to the wet batter and marinate for at least 2 hours or overnight. 2. Prepare the dry batter by whisking together flour, cornstarch, salt, garlic powder, black pepper, and smoked paprika. 3. Remove the chicken from the wet batter, allowing excess to drip off, then coat each strip in the dry batter. 4. Deep-fry the coated chicken strips in hot oil (about 350°F) until golden brown and cooked through, approximately 8-10 minutes, flipping halfway through. 5. Prepare the Cane’s Sauce by whisking together mayonnaise, ketchup,Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, black pepper, salt, and smoked paprika. 6. Serve the crispy chicken fingers with Cane’s Sauce. #canessauce #raisingcanes #friedchicken #chickentenders #Recipe
